attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No available estimate proves B_{ij}=0 for mixed reflected Wilson-loop entries uniformly through collar collapse. The missing Yang-Mills input is a no-new-boundary-renormalization theorem for every finite OS matrix entry, including pair singularities created only by the product \Theta F_i\cdot F_j.
steps: Fix a finite family F_1,\ldots,F_N in the positive-time gauge-invariant core and coefficients c_i. For \delta>0, replace F_i by T_\delta F_i so every insertion is separated from the reflection plane.
At the cutoff level, regulated reflection positivity gives Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jS_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\ge0.

Use the fixed-collar RG convergence topology to pass a,L to the continuum entrywise. Because the cone of positive semidefinite finite matrices is closed, M^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) is positive semidefinite, hence Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\ge0.

For local mirror-flat composites, prove the trace limit by extending smearings by zero across t=0; the collar translation converges in C_c^\infty, so distributional continuity gives S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\to S(\Theta F_i,F_j). This subcase is valid.

Try to repeat the same step for Wilson loops. The individual loop labels C_\delta\to C and D_\delta\to D are not enough, because the OS entry involves the product W_R(\Theta C_\delta)W_R(D_\delta). The reflected pair can form a hairpin, cusp, tangency, or contact singularity at t=0 as \delta\downarrow0.

Introduce the mixed boundary defect B_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}M^\delta_{ij}-M_{ij}. If B=0 for all finite Wilson-loop families, then Q_S(F,c)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\ge0 and the bridge is proved on the Wilson core. If B\ne0, the collar argument proves positivity only for a modified boundary-renormalized matrix, not necessarily for the intended theory.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The fixed-collar closed-cone step is valid, and the local mirror-flat trace step is plausible by distributional continuity, but Wilson-loop products may require pair-dependent renormalization at the reflection plane. Without excluding cusp/hairpin/contact defects, the same-theory condition is unproved.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Mixed reflected Wilson-pair trace modulus for OS cone closure

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity is valid for every finite family F_i in the cutoff positive-time algebra: Q_{a,L}(F,c)\ge0.
For each fixed \delta>0, RG/cutoff convergence controls all reflected matrix entries S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) for finite families in A_+^{core}.
The continuum algebra is locked: F_i and T_\delta F_i are representatives of the same intended observable, not different theories related by a boundary renormalization.
Mixed reflected trace modulus holds entrywise for the finite family: S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\to S(\Theta F_i,F_j) as \delta\downarrow0.
The core algebra is OS-dense in the final positive-time gauge-invariant test algebra with respect to the seminorms induced by finite OS quadratic forms.
definitions: source object: cutoff gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals S_{a,L} on a fixed positive-time observable algebra, with lattice reflection \Theta, regulated reflection-positive quadratic forms Q_{a,L}(F,c), and Wilson-loop renormalizations chosen before the reflection pairing is formed.

target object: continuum Schwinger functional S on the same gauge-invariant OS test algebra whose finite matrices M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) are positive semidefinite, so that OS reconstruction can produce a Hilbert space, vacuum vector, and nonnegative time-translation generator.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via fixed-collar closed-cone passage plus a boundary trace modulus for mixed reflected quadratic forms.

same-theory condition: the collar map T_\delta and the cutoff removal use the same renormalized observables and embeddings at \delta>0 and \delta=0; no extra reflection-plane counterterm, pair-dependent Wilson renormalization, or algebra enlargement is allowed.
A_+^{core}: dense positive-time gauge-invariant algebra generated by mirror-flat local composites and admissible renormalized Wilson-loop observables.
T_\delta: collar-pushing map that moves positive-time observables into t\ge \delta while preserving their labels in the intended continuum algebra.
mixed OS matrix entry: an entry S(\Theta F_i,F_j), not merely the individual expectation of F_i or F_j; this is where reflected Wilson loops can create hairpin or cusp singularities at t=0.

equations.latex: Q_S(T_\delta F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j\,S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\ge0
equations.valid_when: \delta>0 is fixed, the supports are separated from the reflection plane, the RG topology is valid for these reflected entries, and regulated reflection positivity holds before cutoff removal.

equations.label: mixed matrix trace modulus
equations.valid_when: The same renormalized gauge-invariant observable family is used at positive collar and at the plane, with no boundary or pair counterterm.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a pair of Wilson-loop observables C,D for which the individual collar limits are valid but the mixed reflected entry S(W_R(\Theta C_\delta)W_R(D_\delta)) has a nonzero or divergent boundary defect as \delta\downarrow0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the main bridge lemma for the branch. It separates the already-valid closed-cone argument at fixed collar from the Yang-Mills-specific trace problem at the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Mixed reflected collar trace bridge: if fixed-collar reflected quadratic forms are limits of regulated reflection-positive forms and every finite mixed OS matrix entry has a no-new-boundary-renormalization collar trace limit, then the continuum Schwinger functional is OS-positive on the locked gauge-invariant core algebra.

assumptions: Renormalized local-composite Schwinger functions exist as finite-order distributions on ordinary test functions.
The collar shift f\mapsto f_\delta is continuous in C_c^\infty after zero extension across the reflection plane.
Products used in a finite OS matrix entry have already been renormalized away from coincident local insertions, so the only new limit is the reflection-plane collar collapse.
definitions: mirror-flat test function: a smooth compactly supported function on t\ge0 whose normal derivatives of all orders vanish at t=0, so that extension by zero to t<0 is smooth.
local composite core: polynomials in renormalized gauge-invariant local fields such as \operatorname{tr}F_{\mu\nu}F_{\mu\nu}, smeared against mirror-flat test functions.
distributional Schwinger entry: the multilinear distribution obtained by evaluating S on a finite product of renormalized local composite insertions.

equations.label: smooth collar convergence
equations.valid_when: f is extended by zero across t=0 and all normal derivatives vanish at the reflection plane.

equations.label: distributional entry convergence
equations.valid_when: S_n is a finite-order renormalized local-composite Schwinger distribution and the reflected test functions converge in C_c^\infty.

equations.label: local-core trace modulus
equations.valid_when: F_i are finite polynomials in local mirror-flat smeared gauge-invariant composites.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a supposedly renormalized local composite has an unavoidable boundary contact term even for mirror-flat smearing, then the local version of the same-theory trace modulus is false.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a solved model sector and shows the remaining obstruction is not the abstract OS cone but the nonlocal Wilson-loop sector.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Local mirror-flat trace sublemma: for gauge-invariant local composite fields smeared by test functions whose zero extension across t=0 is C^\infty, the mixed collar trace modulus follows from ordinary distributional continuity of the renormalized Schwinger distributions.

assumptions: There is a finite family of Wilson-loop observables F_i for which fixed-collar OS positivity has been obtained.
The entrywise limit of S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) exists after the usual bulk Wilson-loop renormalizations.
The intended continuum matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) is defined without additional boundary data.
definitions: Wilson mixed defect matrix: the entrywise difference between the collar-limit OS matrix and the intended t=0 OS matrix for renormalized Wilson-loop observables.

hairpin limit: a collar collapse in which \Theta C_\delta and D_\delta approach the reflection plane so that the reflected product develops a cusp, tangency, shared endpoint, or near-parallel singular region.
same-theory falsifier: a defect that can be removed only by adding a reflection-plane counterterm, changing Wilson-loop renormalization, or adjoining a new boundary observable.

equations.valid_when: The positivity bridge is claimed for the original continuum Schwinger functional rather than a boundary-renormalized theory.

equations.valid_when: The nonzero defect is not positive-order dominated and hence can turn the intended OS quadratic form negative.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find C,D for which I_\delta or its nonperturbative analog contains an uncancelled \log\delta, power divergence, or finite factor not equal to one after ordinary bulk Wilson-loop renormalization.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the vague worry about Wilson loops into a concrete falsifier search: compute or bound the mixed defect matrix, not just the renormalization of single loops.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Wilson pair boundary-defect falsifier criterion: a nonzero mixed reflected boundary defect for a finite Wilson-loop OS matrix falsifies the same-theory positivity bridge, even if a modified boundary-renormalized matrix remains positive.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a one-loop or nonperturbative Wilson hairpin calculation exhibits an unavoidable mixed boundary defect after ordinary bulk renormalization, because then the current same-theory OS bridge cannot work.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one obtains a uniform estimate |S(W_R(\Theta C_\delta)W_R(D_\delta))-S(W_R(\Theta C)W_R(D))|\le\omega_{C,D}(\delta) for a Wilson-loop core, plus OS density of that core in the locked gauge-invariant algebra.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a precise non-tautological target: prove or falsify the mixed Wilson-pair no-boundary-renormalization trace modulus. This is sharper than the previous closed-cone topology question and directly tests the controlled interface.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge is now decomposed into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone theorem plus the substantive mixed reflected trace theorem. The formal part is valid; the Wilson-pair trace is the bottleneck.

The local mirror-flat composite sector appears compatible with distributional trace continuity. The Wilson-loop sector must be restricted to loops for which all mixed OS pairings have zero boundary defect, or else the algebra is not same-theory.
The topology must control not only separated reflected probes but also the limit of their OS matrix entries as the collar width tends to zero. Fixed-collar convergence alone is insufficient.

Prove that ordinary bulk Wilson-loop renormalization removes all divergences in W_R(\Theta C_\delta)W_R(D_\delta) uniformly as reflected supports collide with the plane, with no cusp or hairpin counterterm.

falsifiers: A concrete falsifier would be a pair of renormalized Wilson loops C,D such that S(W_R(\Theta C_\delta)W_R(D_\delta)) has an uncancelled \log\delta or power divergence as \delta\downarrow0 after all ordinary bulk loop renormalizations.
A finite nonunit boundary factor B_{C,D}\ne0 is also a falsifier of the same-theory bridge, even if it preserves positivity after redefining a boundary Wilson observable.
The RG topology may be valid for every fixed collar \delta>0 but fail to provide estimates uniform enough to take \delta\downarrow0 in reflected Wilson pairings.

Gauge-invariant test algebra mismatch: adding a hairpin counterterm or boundary Wilson-loop generator can make the OS cone closed for a different theory, not for the intended Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.

Order-of-limits obstruction: if the continuum limit exists only with \delta/a fixed, or if taking a\downarrow0 before \delta\downarrow0 differs from the intended observable at \delta=0, then the bridge fails.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 179 upgrades the obstruction from single-loop trace continuity to finite OS matrix trace continuity. The valid part of the bridge is short: fixed-collar reflection positivity passes by closedness, and local mirror-flat composites pass to the plane by distributional continuity. The hard Yang-Mills question is whether mixed reflected Wilson products acquire a boundary defect as \Theta C_\delta and D_\delta collide at t=0. A nonzero mixed defect is a same-theory falsifier: it may still leave a positive boundary-renormalized theory, but it does not prove OS positivity for the intended continuum Schwinger functions.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the perturbative one-loop cross integral for a mirror hairpin pair of smooth Wilson loops whose collars approach t=0. Check whether ordinary perimeter/corner renormalizations cancel all \delta-dependent terms in I_\delta(C,D), or whether a residual cusp/hairpin coefficient remains as the first explicit falsifier of the same-theory mixed trace modulus.
